prompt: A paperclip is strongly attracted to a magnet, while an aluminium can is barely affected. The key difference inside the iron of the paperclip is that iron:

options.text: Contains tiny permanent electric charges that magnets pull on
Is heavier, and magnets attract heavy metals
Has magnetic domains — regions whose atomic magnetic fields can line up together, reinforcing each other
Conducts electricity, and all good conductors are strongly magnetic

explanation: Ferromagnetic materials such as iron have domains in which many atoms' magnetic moments are aligned. An external field rotates more domains into alignment, producing a strong combined attraction, unlike weakly magnetic aluminium.
